children.translated_text: Ipv: Cognitions of relation such as 'the king's man' have as their object internally the unity through mutual connection, and externally the difference of the relata. //
Conceptions apprehend
the unity of form of manifestations of <s>jāti</s> (universal) and <s>dravya</s> (substance) even externally,
and also the difference of parts within individuals
[—this they apprehend].

children.text: Ipv: gavaś caitra iti ca matayo bahir api gomātraikaghanapuruṣaviśeṣākārābhāsaikyaṃ svalakṣaṇāvayavābhāsabahutvaṃ ca parāmṛśanti //
children.translated_text: Ipv: Cognitions such as 'cows' and '<s>Caitra</s>' reflectively grasp both the unity of the appearance of the form of the single dense universal cow-nature or the particular form of a person externally, and the multiplicity of <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>-part-manifestations (appearances of particular components). //
The coordination of the <s>kārakas</s> (syntactic factors),
which is the object of the reflective awareness of action,
and the cognition of direction and the like, which has as its object
the connection in the form of the delimited and the delimiter—

children.text: Vṛ: kāṣṭhasthalīdevadattaudanānāṃ pacatīty antaḥsamanvayād bahirbhedāc caikānekaviṣayā kriyāmatiḥ / deśakālakramo 'pi bhāvānām avadhyavadhimadrūpāṇām anyonyāpekṣaḥ saṃbandhabheda eva tathaivaikānekamayaḥ / jātidravyakriyāsaṃkhyādimatayaḥ sarvā eva saṃbandhaviśeṣasamavāyaviṣayā eva //
children.translated_text: Vṛ: The cognition of action, such as 'he cooks,' having as its object both the unity through internal coordination and the external difference of wood, ground, <s>Devadatta</s>, and rice, pertains to what is both one and many. The sequence of place and time of entities too, in the form of the delimited and the delimiter, is nothing but a variety of relation that depends on mutual reference, and is likewise composed of unity and multiplicity. Cognitions of universal, substance, action, number, and the like—all have as their object precisely particular varieties of relation and <s>samavāya</s> (inherence). //
In just this way, the accomplishment of purpose would occur
for the <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower) who desires effective action—
by means of an object possessing [both] difference and non-difference;
therefore, such [cognition] is not erroneous.

children.text: Ipv: ekānekarūpair eva kriyādibhir evam ābhāsānuguṇyarūpaḥ pramātus tadarthino 'rthakriyāsaṃvādaḥ / tato na tadbuddhayo bhrāntāḥ //
children.translated_text: Ipv: Through actions and the like, which are precisely of the form of unity-and-multiplicity, there is the correspondence of effective action (<s>arthakriyā</s>) for the <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower) who desires that—conforming to the manifestations. Therefore those cognitions are not erroneous. //
Thus ends the second lesson in the Chapter on Action. //
Third lesson. //
'This is such'—in accordance with that
by which the object is firmly established,
that is <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge); and that too
is a self-manifestation, a fresh arising.
That same [manifestation], being internally of the nature of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>),
pertaining to an object undifferentiated by place, time, and the like,
the object of a single designation—
[this] is <s>pramiti</s> (valid cognition) regarding the object, uncontradicted.

children.text: Ipv: yadāyattā hi vastunaḥ svarūpeṇa nityatāviśeṣaṇair vā vyavasthāpyamānatā sa pramātuḥ svatvenāpūrvavastvābhāsaiva sthitaḥ pramāṇam / sa eva cābhāso 'yam iti nitya iti vā tathaiva pṛthaktayābhinavatvena ca pramātary uparūḍho vimarśarūpatām āpanno vimarśabhedānusāryaikaikaśabdavācye pṛthakpṛthag eva tiraskṛtadeśādibhede tasminn ābhāta eva sāmānyarūpe vastuni svakārthakriyāprāpte pramāṇāntareṇābādhitasthairyā pramitiḥ pramātṛvyāpāraḥ //
children.translated_text: Ipv: That upon which depends the object's being established in its own form or through qualifiers such as permanence—that, for the <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower), is nothing but the manifestation of a novel object as one's own, and this constitutes <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge). And that very manifestation, mounted upon the knower as 'this' or as 'permanent,' thus separately and with novelty, having attained the form of <s>vimarśa</s> (reflective awareness), expressible by individual words following the distinctions of reflective awareness, with difference of place and the like concealed—in that very object which has manifested as having a universal form, having attained its own purpose of effective action, with its stability uncontradicted by another <s>pramāṇa</s>—is <s>pramiti</s> (valid cognition), the activity of the <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower). //
According to one's inclination, according to one's need,
according to one's expertise, the manifestation
is differentiated even regarding a single object—
[an object] established through synthesis (<s>anusaṃdhāna</s>).

children.text: Ipv: ekasminn eva caikapratyavamarśasāmarthyopapādite vastuni svecchāvaśād arthitvānurodhād vā naipuṇyavaśād vāvabhāsabhedaḥ //
children.translated_text: Ipv: Regarding a single object, established through the capacity of a unitary reflective recognition (<s>pratyavamarśa</s>), there is differentiation of manifestation by the force of one's own will, or in accordance with one's need, or by the force of one's skill. //
For example:
By [appearances such as] long, round, tall, human,
smoke, sandalwood, and the like,
manifestations are differentiated
[even of objects] undifferentiated by place and time.
Likewise, existent, pot, substance,
golden, brilliant, and the like—
these differentiated manifestations, producing distinct effective actions,
are the ground for verbal expression (<s>dhvani</s>).

children.text:
Ipv: ekasminn eva ghaṭādav arthe 'vadhitsāvaśād dīrghatā tryaśratāpārimāṇḍalyādi vābhāti, cihnavyavadhānachāyāmātrārthitāyāṃ puruṣa evordhvatāmātraṃ pratibhāti, tatkāryārthitāyāṃ tu nyakṣeṇekṣamāṇasya puruṣaḥ / dhūmamātram eva kasya cid ābhāsate, tadvidas tu tārṇatādi maṇirūpyādiviśeṣa iva / sa ca tathā bhidyamāno 'pi deśakālabhedaṃ na spṛśati / tathaiva ghaṭa eva san nityābhāso 'nyādṛg eva paṭādyanantāśeṣārthasādhāra~aḥ sattāmātrasādhyasatparāmarśādyarthakriyākārī, tatraiva ghaṭa iti cābhāso 'ntarbahiṣkaraṇajñeyaḥ pṛthubudhnodarākārārthasāmānyo 'nya eva yaḥ paṭādiṣu nāsti, kāñcana iti cāparo yo mṛṇmayādiṣu nāsti sa ca tathārthitādivaśād aindriyaka eva jāyate / ekaikaś cāsav ābhāsa ekaikena śabdena vyavahārārthaṃ
tattanniyatārthakriyārthibhir abhidhīyate, ghaṭa iti na sattābhidhīyate na ca kāñcana iti ghaṭābhāsaḥ / caitra iti bālyādisādhāraṇo deśādirahitas tathaiva ca / tato 'rthakriyā bhinnā //
children.translated_text: Ipv: Regarding one and the same object such as a pot, depending on the desire to know, longness, triangularity, roundness, and the like are manifested; when only a sign, intervening shadow, or mere outline is desired, merely the tallness of a person appears; but when one desires its effect, the person [appears] to one looking carefully. For someone, mere smoke alone is manifested, but for one who knows it, [the specific nature such as] being of grass and so on [appears], just as a specific [nature] of gems and silver. And even though differentiated thus, it does not touch the difference of place and time. Likewise, in the very same pot, the manifestation 'existent'—permanent, of a different character, common to all objects such as cloth without exception—produces effective actions such as the reflective awareness of the existent, which are accomplished by mere existence alone. And there the manifestation 'this is a pot' is to be known through both inner and outer faculties, being a universal of the form of a broad-bottomed and bellied object, which is other [than what is found] in cloth and the like. And 'golden' is yet another [manifestation] which does not exist in those made of clay and so on—and this arises in sensory [cognition] alone, in accordance with desire and the like. And each of these manifestations is designated by a single word by those desiring the specific effective action determined by each—'pot' does not designate existence, nor does 'golden' [designate] the pot-manifestation. '<s>Caitra</s>' [designates what is] common to childhood and other [stages], devoid of place and the like, and likewise. Therefore, effective action is differentiated. //
The specific effective action of objects
arises from the differentiation of manifestations;
yet through the manifestation of <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-referentiality),
[objects are cognized as] non-different.

children.text: Ipv: ekasminn eva svalakṣaṇe pratyābhāsaṃ niyatiśaktyā kāryaṃ niyamitaṃ tathābhūtānekakāryakṛdābhāsabhedādhikaraṇam ekaṃ ca / sāmānādhikaraṇyābhāsavaśād vastu / anekasyaikatā hi sāmānādhikaraṇyam //
children.translated_text: Ipv: In one and the same <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), with each manifestation the effect is determined by the power of regularity (<s>niyati-śakti</s>); and it is a single substratum of manifestation-differences that produce multiple such effects. Through the manifestation of <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-referentiality), [it is cognized as] a [single] object. For the unity of the many is indeed <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>. //
Just as the lights of separate lamps
or the streams [merging] in the ocean—
so for non-contradictory manifestations,
the cognition of unity has a single effect.

children.text: Ipv: bhinnāḥ pradīpaprabhā avibhāgenāvabhāsante nadīpravāhāś ca sindhubuddhau pānake ca te te rasās, tathā śauklyamahattvapaṭatvādyavabhāsāḥ parasparānupraveśakṣamāḥ, na tu nīlapītādyavabhāsās tattadekakāryaikadravyābhāsabhāvena kalpante pratyakṣa eva / tad etat sāmānādhikaraṇyam //
children.translated_text: Ipv: The separate lights of lamps appear without distinction, and the currents of rivers [merge] in the cognition of the ocean, and in a beverage the various flavors—likewise, manifestations such as whiteness, largeness, cloth-ness, and the like are capable of mutual interpenetration; but manifestations such as blue and yellow do not serve as a single effect or single substance manifestation—this is directly perceived. This indeed is <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-referentiality). //
There, regarding fire and the like as unparticularized,
the heat that is [both] effect and cause,
the nature of being the referent of such-and-such words, and so on—
[all] are understood from a single <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge).

children.text: Ipv: kadā cid deśādisahabhāvāvachinnasvalakṣaṇarūpaviśeṣatyāgenaikasāmānyarūpāgnyābhāsamātra eva trailokyatraikālyagāmitvena nijapramāṇād ekasmād eva viśiṣṭakāryakāraṇatoṣṇordhvabhāg agniśabdavācyatādisvabhāvasiddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: Ipv: Sometimes, by relinquishing the particular form of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) delimited by coexistence with place and the like, through the mere manifestation of fire in a single universal form alone—extending across the three worlds and three times—from its own single <s>pramāṇa</s> alone, there is the establishment of the nature [of fire] as producing specific effects, as being a cause, as being hot, as tending upward, as being denoted by the word 'fire,' and so on. //
But that [effective action] regarding the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular)
differentiated by perception of place and the like—
the activity pertaining to the present moment
of one who desires [a specific object] is [also] from inference.

children.text: Ipv: kāyapravṛttiḥ puno deśakālādipratyakṣabhedasāhityena svalakṣaṇa eva tadarthitayā pramāṇasamūhād eva / anumānād api dharmipratyakṣaviśiṣṭād eva pravṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: Ipv: Bodily activity, however, is directed toward the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) alone, accompanied by perceptual differentiation of place, time, and the like, out of desire for that, from the totality of <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of knowledge). Even from inference, activity proceeds only as qualified by the perception of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>). //
Through the nature of objects as far and near,
as imperceptible and perceptible,
as external and internal, or through defects
of the illuminating [faculty], or otherwise—
even when there is a difference in the shade of manifestation,
the unity [of the object] is unimpeded
due to the principal manifestation,
which is called the single reflective recognition (<s>pratyavamarśa</s>).

children.text: Ipv: dūrāntikādisphuṭāsphuṭatvādinā bahirantaścaratvena vābhāsasya cchāyāmātrabhede 'pi tanmukhyasvabhāvarūpapratyavamarśaikyād arthānām aikyam abādhitam //
children.translated_text: Ipv: Even when there is a mere difference of shade in the manifestation due to clear and unclear [perception] arising from far and near distance, or from [the object's] being external and internal—the unity of objects is uncontradicted, owing to the identity of the reflective recognition of the principal intrinsic nature of that [manifestation]. //
Moreover, <s>arthakriyā</s> (effective action) is innate;
it is not [intrinsic] to objects; by the will of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord)
it is regulated. For that reason,
its otherness [i.e., unreality] does not follow from the absence of [external] action.

children.text: Ipv: ullekhaghaṭādīnāṃ bāhyārthakriyāvirahe 'pi ghaṭāditayaiva, asvabhāvikatvāt tasyā īśvareṇa pratyābhāsaṃ niyamitāyāḥ //
children.translated_text: Ipv: Even in the absence of external effective action for imagined pots and the like, [they are cognized] precisely as pots and so on, because that [effective action] is not intrinsic [to them] but is regulated by <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) for each manifestation. //
Even when there is a single reflective awareness of silver
in nacre, silver does not persist [there],
due to the non-correspondence of the adventitious condition and location;
in [the case of] the double moon too, the sky [shows it to be] otherwise.

children.text: Ipv: rajate śuktau ca rajatāvamarśaikyena rajatatve 'pi punaḥ śuktideśasaṅgatibādhenopādhisaṃvādābhāvāt tadbuddhir asthairyād bhrāntā / dvicandre 'pi nabhodeśāsaṃvādān mithyā //
children.translated_text: Ipv: Even though there is identity of the reflective awareness of silver in both silver and nacre, and hence silver-ness [in both], nevertheless, because of the contradiction with the location of nacre and the absence of correspondence of the adventitious condition (<s>upādhi</s>), that cognition is erroneous due to its instability. In the case of the double moon too, it is false due to the non-correspondence with the location of the sky. //
Through qualities such as sound and the like, there is difference,
and through universals (<s>jāti</s>) and the like, non-difference
of entities—thus, [both are established]
in a single <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower).

children.text: Ipv: bhāvānāṃ śabdarūpasaṃsthānādinā bhedākṣepo jātyādinā caikatākṣepo 'nubhūyamānaḥ pramātraikye ghaṭate / anyonyabhedavyavasthāpy anusaṃdhānāyattā //
children.translated_text: Ipv: The suggestion of difference in entities through sound, form, shape, and the like, and the suggestion of unity through universals (<s>jāti</s>) and the like—as experienced—is tenable only given the unity of the <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower). The establishment of mutual difference too depends on synthesis (<s>anusaṃdhāna</s>). //
In <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), who is supremely real,
resembling an even wall-surface,
touched by contradictory manifestations,
variegated with the diversity of the universe—
in the ancient <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower),
whose form is always manifest—
what [need is there for] <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge)? A new manifestation
[is already] a portion of all <s>pramiti</s> (valid cognition).

children.text: Ipv: apūrvābhāsasyāsiddhavastusādhanān nityāvabhāsinaḥ pramātur na pramāṇopayogaḥ / tattannavābhāsānāṃ tattatpramāṇatvāt kāmaṃ sa pramāṇam anyasya syān na tu svātmanaḥ sadā siddhasya, kevalaṃ vibhuḥ pramitau svātantryāt pramātaiva / te te vicitrā viśvābhāsās tasmin sthāyini vaicitryeṇopapadyante / tad icchāto 'parāvabhāsamānārthānāṃ tatsārasvarūpabhraṃśe māyāśaktivaśād unmajjananimajjane, tattvatas tasyaivāparādhīnā sattā sadātanī viruddhaprākpradhvaṃsābhāvādiprayogāt, sa api yāvad upadiśyate bhāvābhāvābhyāṃ tāvat sa eva pramātṛtāṃ bhajata upadidikṣor abhāvād upadeśānupapatteḥ //
children.translated_text: Ipv: For [the Lord] who is eternally manifest, there is no need for <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) as a means to establish an unestablished object through a novel manifestation. Since each novel manifestation constitutes the respective <s>pramāṇa</s>, it may well be a <s>pramāṇa</s> for another, but not for one's own Self which is always established. He is simply the all-pervading <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower) itself in cognition, by virtue of [His] sovereignty. The various and diverse universal manifestations are tenable in that abiding [Self] through variety. Through His will, for objects not otherwise manifesting—by the power of <s>Māyā-śakti</s>, [there is] emergence and submergence in the loss of their essential nature as His essence; but in reality, His existence is eternal and dependent on no other, as evidenced by the usage of contradictory [terms such as] prior non-existence, destruction, and absence. And even as long as this is being taught, since there is no one to teach who is not [already] partaking of both being and non-being, He alone assumes the status of <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower), for in the absence of one who wishes to learn, instruction would be impossible. //
What was simply not set forth before here
merely due to the force of delusion—
the discourse of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) and the like
is set forth through the revelation of [His] powers.

children.text: Ipv: māyāvyāmohavaśāt kevalam asminn ātmani pramātṛrūpe śiveśvarādivyavahāro yo na pravartitaḥ sa śuddhasvātantryādihetupradarśanena bhāvanādyupadeśāya sādhyate //
children.translated_text: Ipv: Merely due to the delusion of <s>Māyā</s>, that discourse of <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and the like which was not set forth regarding this Self, which is of the nature of the <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower)—that is accomplished through the demonstration of the reasons [such as] pure sovereignty and the like, for the purpose of instruction in contemplative practice (<s>bhāvanā</s>) and the like. //
Thus ends the third lesson in the Chapter on Action. //
And this [Lord], because of possessing infinite powers,
manifests these
entities by the force of [His] will—
this is [His] <s>kriyā</s> (action), His creatorship.

children.text: Ipv: pramātā cidrūpo 'nantaśaktir īśvaraḥ svecchāvaśāt tathā tān bhāvān ābhāsayet / saiva cecchāśaktir nirmātṛtākhyā kriyā tasya //
children.translated_text: Ipv: The <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower), whose nature is consciousness and who possesses infinite powers, is <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). By the force of His own will, He would thus manifest those entities. And that <s>icchā-śakti</s> (power of will) itself is the <s>kriyā</s> (action) called creatorship that belongs to Him. //
But an insentient [entity] does not have that power—
[namely,] the existence that [brings] what is non-existent into existence;
causality is nothing but
the nature of agency and objecthood (<s>kartṛ-karmatva</s>).

children.text: Ipv: jaḍaṃ pradhānaparamāṇubījādi tu na śaktam asato nirmāṇe, kartṛtvam eva hi kāraṇatvaṃ karmataiva ca kāryatvaṃ na tv anyat //
children.translated_text: Ipv: An insentient [principle] such as <s>Pradhāna</s>, atoms, or seeds is not capable of creating what is non-existent. For causality is nothing but agency, and being an effect is nothing but objecthood—there is nothing else. //
What is non-existent—a connection with the non-existent is absurd;
non-existence cannot have the nature of existence.
And for what [already] exists, if existence is not newly acquired,
then what purpose [would creation serve]?—so it is argued.
[Yet] causality in the world
consists in the internal transformation [of what exists]—
its becoming cognizable by both [sets of] faculties
[happens] through the power of some [agent].

children.text: Ipv: asataḥ satsvabhāvatā viruddhā sataś ca siddhā / siddhasyaivāntarbāhyāntaḥkaraṇadvayīvedyatāpādanam īśvareṇotpādanam //
children.translated_text: Ipv: The non-existent having the nature of the existent is contradictory, while for the existent it is [already] established. The bringing about of the already-established [entity's] cognizability by the dyad of outer and inner faculties is what <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) [accomplishes as] creation. //
Thus this one <s>kriyā</s> (action),
consisting of sequential internal and external existence,
has been established as belonging to a single [agent]
who is capable of both forms.

children.text: Ipv: saiṣā kriyāntarbahiḥsthitirūpatayā sakramāpy ekasya svasaṃvitsiddhasya kartur ābhāsachāyābhede 'py aikyena pratyavamṛśyasya karmaṇaś caikasya saṃnaṃdhinī tadabhinnāśrayatvād ekatvena sādhitā //
children.translated_text: Ipv: This <s>kriyā</s> (action), having the form of internal and external existence and being sequential, has been established as one—[belonging to] a single agent established through self-awareness, and to a single object reflectively recognized as identical even amid differences of manifestation-shade—because it has a non-different substratum and is thus established as one. //
Externally, that which is its effect—
what was internal, with reference to that—
and with reference to the <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower), the dual
external and internal existence has been stated.

children.text: Ipv: arthasya bāhyatāpādanaṃ kāryatvaṃ, tato bāhyatā kāryatā caikāpekṣayā pramātaram apekṣya cāntarbahirvyavahāraḥ / tatas tasyaiva kāryam //
children.translated_text: Ipv: The bringing about of the object's externality is its being an effect; thus externality and effecthood [are understood] with reference to one [the object], and the discourse of internal and external is with reference to the <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower). Therefore, the effect belongs to that [knower] alone. //
The <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower) alone is therefore the cause;
and He, in the state of the two manifestations,
abides as one with the effect—
thus <s>kriyā</s> (action) of a single [agent] has been proclaimed.

children.text: Ipv: evaṃ pramātaiva kāraṇaṃ sa ca bāhyāntarakāryābhāsakrame 'py eka evety evam apy ekasya kartuḥ siddhā kriyā //
children.translated_text: Ipv: Thus the <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower) alone is the cause, and He is one even in the sequence of external and internal manifestation of the effect—thus action has been established as belonging to a single agent. //
For this very reason, even for a sprout,
<s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) is accepted as the efficient cause;
for something else, such as a seed,
causality is not tenable.

children.text: Ipv: bāhyābhāsatāpādanam utpādanam iti cidrūpasyaiva kāraṇatā tato 'ṅkurādau nimittakāraṇatveśvaraḥ kaiś cid iṣṭo, na cāpi bījāder jaḍasya kāraṇatā niranusaṃdhānasya yuktā //
children.translated_text: Ipv: Bringing about external manifestation is creation—hence causality belongs to [that which is] of the nature of consciousness alone. Therefore, <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) is accepted by some as the efficient cause (<s>nimitta-kāraṇa</s>) even for a sprout and the like. And the causality of an insentient [entity] such as a seed, which lacks synthesis (<s>anusaṃdhāna</s>), is not tenable. //
For example, a potter—
by the arrangement that is [his] sovereignty alone—
through the successive operations upon clay and the like,
would produce a pot.

children.text: Ipv: kumbhakārarūpe pramātari kāraṇe sthite 'pi mṛdādisaṃskārāpekṣā ghaṭasyeśvarakṛtaniyatisaṃjñamaryādayā na svabhāvena //
children.translated_text: Ipv: Even when the <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower) in the form of the potter is established as the cause, the dependence on the processing of clay and the like for the pot [exists] by the convention called the regularity established by <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord)—not by intrinsic nature. //
Even for <s>yogins</s>, without clay or seed,
by the force of will alone,
pots and the like are produced,
producing stable and genuine effective action.

children.text: Ipv: mṛdādyanapekṣasya yoginām icchāmātreṇa ghaṭādeḥ sthirasya ghaṭādyarthakriyākāriṇaś ca nirvṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: Ipv: Without depending on clay and the like, by the mere will of <s>yogins</s>, pots and the like come into being—stable and capable of producing the effective action proper to pots and so on. //
In the absence of ascertainment by another <s>pramāṇa</s>
of the non-existence of yogic creation,
[the argument that] the effect, the cause, or the intrinsic nature—
born from the very source of [their] origination—[proves this, is] a fallacious reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>).

children.text: Ipv: ata eva kāryaṃ svabhāvo vā tadutpattigarbho yoginirmitatvābhāvaniścayābhāve hetvābhāsaḥ / tanniścaye puna īśvaraniyatyapekṣayā hetutā syāt //
children.translated_text: Ipv: For this very reason, the effect, or the intrinsic nature containing [within it] its origination, is a fallacious reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) in the absence of ascertainment of the non-existence of yogic creation. But if that [non-existence] were ascertained, then causality would [still] require the regularity established by <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). //
Furthermore, the unity of each and every <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower)
there may arise from a fire-appearance and so on;
even from the indirect ruler,
a new smoke-appearance and so forth
may arise. The effect, as the invariable
indicator, from the appearance belonging to another knower—
its appearance arises from that very appearance
of the ruler, which is different.

children.text: Ipv: avahnyābhāsasphuraṇapūrvako 'pi jāyamāno dhūmābhāso dūrādau niyatiśaktyā kṛtasāmarthyād agnyābhāsād eva taddeśagatatattatpramātrantarasādhāraṇāt tasyaiva sa avyabhicāreṇa gamako, jātarūḍhas tu dhūmābhāsas tadvahnyābhāsasyātyantaparikṣayāt tattatpramātrantaragād dhūmābhāsād eva parokṣād api pūrvavat kṛtādhipatyāt //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: Even the smoke-appearance that arises without the prior manifestation of a fire-appearance—as when perceived from afar—is an indicator exclusively of the fire-appearance, which is common to the various other knowers present at that location, empowered by the power of <s>niyati</s> (necessity). But the smoke-appearance that has already arisen and become established, since the fire-appearance has completely perished for it, indicates from the indirect smoke-appearance belonging to other knowers, which, as before, has been made the ruler. //
"When this exists, that exists"—
this causal relation too
is untenable for inert things
that are devoid of mutual reference.

children.text: Ipv: asmin satīdaṃ bhavatīti niyataṃ paurvāparyaṃ kṛttikārohinyudayayor akāryakāraṇayor apy astīti pūrvasya sāmarthye parasya satteti syāt kāryakāraṇabhāvas, tac cāpekṣārahitānāṃ jāḍānāṃ na yuktam / etāvad etat syāt pūrvasya sāmarthyaṃ parasya sattā na caivaṃ kiṃcid uktaṃ syān na ca pūrvasya sāmarthyalakṣaṇaḥ svabhāvaḥ parasattārūpaḥ //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: 'When this exists, that comes to be'—this fixed sequence exists even between the rising of the Pleiades and Rohiṇī, which are not cause and effect. So this could mean: the capacity of the prior and the existence of the subsequent constitute causality. But that is not tenable for inert things devoid of mutual reference. This much it would be: 'the capacity of the prior, the existence of the subsequent'—but nothing is thereby truly said; nor is the essential nature of the prior, characterized by capacity, of the form of the subsequent's existence. //
For those that rest solely in their own nature,
that are devoid of interconnection—
even in the case of existence and non-existence,
the meaning of the locative case cannot be postulated.

children.text: Ipv: sad asad vā kāryaṃ kāraṇam apy ātmaparyavasitaṃ jaḍam anusandhānaśūnyaṃ nānyāpekṣasvabhāvaṃ tataś ca nātra pradhānāpekṣāmayo guṇavibhaktyartho ghaṭate //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: Whether the effect is existent or non-existent, and the cause too—if inert and terminating in its own self, empty of interconnection—it is not of the nature of depending on another. Therefore the meaning of the subordinate-dependent case expressing the quality-substance relation does not apply here. //
Therefore, the meaning of the case-relation,
resting solely in a single knower,
called the relation of action and instrument,
is the proper connection of entities.

children.text: Ipv: ekapramātṛsaṃlagnas tu kriyākārakabhāvākhyo vibhaktyartho bhūmibījodakādīnāṃ samanvayo yukto na tu śuṣko 'nyaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: The meaning of the case-relation, connected to a single knower, called the relation of action and instrument—the connection of earth, seed, water, and so on—is proper; not any dry, separate causal relation. //
If cause and effect had each other's nature,
there would be identity alone;
for in difference,
there would be no mutual nature at all.

children.text: Ipv: kāryakāraṇayor anyonyarūpatve 'py ekataiva syān na tadbhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: If cause and effect had each other's nature, there would be identity alone, not that relation. //
And the differentiation of a single entity
is action, following temporal sequence;
thus there would be agenthood—
of one who transforms accordingly through it.

children.text: Ipv: ekasvabhāvasya bhedena sthitiḥ pariṇāmaḥ kālakalitaḥ kriyaiva, tataḥ pariṇāme svatantrasya śāktimataḥ kartṛtaiva hetunā //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: The existence of one of a single nature in a state of differentiation is transformation, associated with time—that is action itself. Therefore, in transformation, there is agenthood of the independent one who possesses powers, by reason of that. //
But this is not tenable for the inert,
due to the contradiction of difference and non-difference;
through the difference of appearances in a single
entity of the nature of consciousness, however, it is tenable.

children.text: Ipv: jaḍasyābhinnātmano bhedenāvasthiter virodhād ayuktaṃ, svacche cidātmany ekasminn evam anekapratibimbadhāraṇenāvirodhād yujyate //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: For the inert, whose nature is undifferentiated, existence in a state of differentiation involves contradiction and is thus untenable. In a single transparent entity of the nature of consciousness, however, due to the absence of contradiction in bearing multiple reflections, it is tenable. //
Even given the real unity of consciousness,
there would be no action between things differing in appearance
without the reflective awareness of unity
characterized by the will to act.

children.text: Ipv: ekasmiñ cittattve 'py akasmād ābhāsabhedo na ghaṭate, na ca tatra kriyātvam / yadā tu sa cidātmā tathācikīrṣayā parāmṛśan bahir ābhāsayati tadā tad upapadyate / jaḍasyāpy asti bhavatīty asyām api sattākriyāyāṃ bubhūṣāyogena svātantryābhāvād akartṛtvaṃ, tena pramātaiva taṃ bhāvayati tena tena vā himācalādinā rūpeṇa sa bhavatīty atra paramārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: Even in the one reality of consciousness, a difference of appearances would not arise without cause, nor would there be the nature of action in it. But when that conscious Self, reflecting through the will to act in that manner, manifests externally, then it is tenable. Even for the inert, in this very activity of existence—'it is, it becomes'—there is non-agenthood due to the absence of freedom through the desire to become. Therefore, it is the knower alone who brings it into being, or it becomes in this or that form, such as the Himalaya—this is the ultimate truth. //
Thus, for one who wishes to abide in this manner
as the Self of the world of appearances such as pots and cloths,
the will alone is the causality,
the agenthood, and the action.

children.text: Ipv: cidvapuṣaḥ svatantrasya viśvātmanā sthātum icchaiva jagat prati kāraṇatā kartṛtārūpā saiva kriyāśaktiḥ / evaṃ cidrūpasyaikasya kartur eva cikīrṣākhyā kriyā mukhyā, nākartṛkaṃ karmāsti karmādīnāṃ kartṛmukhenopacārataḥ //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: For the independent one of the nature of consciousness, the will to exist as the universal Self is the causality toward the world—that which has the nature of agenthood is itself the power of action. Thus, for one who is of the nature of consciousness, a single agent, the primary action is the will called 'the desire to act'; there is no action without an agent; and instruments and the rest are attributed with agenthood figuratively, through the agent. //
Thus ends the fourth lesson in the Chapter on Action. //
Thus ends the Chapter on Action. //
3. Chapter on Scriptural Testimony (<s>Āgama</s>) //
3.1 First Lesson //
Thus, the activity that is both internal and external,
action following temporal sequence,
belongs to the knower alone; those two—
knowledge and action—are inseparable from each other.

children.text: Ipv: pramātur antaḥsthitasyātmano bahiṣkāra eva kramānugatā kriyeti parasparāvirahite tasya jñānakriye //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: The very externalization of the knower's Self, which abides internally, following temporal sequence, is action. Thus knowledge and action are inseparable from one another for that knower. //
However, from the predominance of the internal state,
the <s>tattva</s> (reality) called <s>Sadāśiva</s> comes first;
and when the external state predominates,
subsequently comes the <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord) <s>tattva</s>.

children.text: Ipv: īśitur antarbahiḥsthitav antarbhāvaprādhānye punaḥ sādākhyaṃ tattvam, aparaṃ bahirbhāvodrekād aiśvaram //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: For the ruler, in the states of internal and external abiding, when the internal state predominates, there is the <s>tattva</s> called <s>Sadāśiva</s>; the other, from the predominance of the external state, is the <s>Aiśvara</s> (Lordly) <s>tattva</s>. //
<s>Īśvara</s> is the outward opening,
<s>Sadāśiva</s> the inward closing;
and the co-predication
of the 'I'-consciousness and 'this'-consciousness

children.text: Ipv: unmeṣanimeṣau bahirantaḥsthitī eveśvarasadāśivau, bāhyāntarayor vedyavedakayor ekacinmātraviśrānter abhedāt sāmānādhikaraṇyenedaṃ viśvam aham iti viśvātmano matiḥ śuddhavidyā //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: Opening and closing are the external and internal states themselves—<s>Īśvara</s> and <s>Sadāśiva</s>. Due to the non-difference of the external and internal, the known and the knower, resting in pure consciousness alone, the cognition through co-predication 'this universe is I' of the universal Self is <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge). //
Of entities that have assumed the nature of 'this,'
that have entered the domain of the knowable—
because of their essence being awareness,
through seeing things as they truly are,

children.text: Ipv: binnavedyabhūmav idantayā dṛśyatām āpāditānām api bhāvānāṃ cinmātrasāratvād aham idam iti tattvapratipattiḥ śuddhatājñāptiḥ //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: Even of entities brought to the status of objectivity as 'this' in the differentiated domain of the knowable, because their essence is pure consciousness, there is the realization 'I am this'—the knowledge of the <s>tattva</s> (reality), the communication of purity. //
Here, the inferiority of entities
comes from their appearing as non-Self;
their superiority from the concealment by the 'I'-sense;
for that state is both higher and lower.

children.text: Ipv: atredaṃtāmater aparatvam ahaṃtayā sarvasya vedyasyācchādanāt parateti parāparāvasthaiṣā //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: Here, in the cognition of 'this'-ness, there is inferiority; from the concealment of everything knowable by the 'I'-sense, there is superiority. Thus this is a state of both higher and lower. //
The very cognition of difference in entities,
which belongs to the agent of the nature of awareness—
that, through the power of <s>Māyā</s> alone, is <s>Vidyā</s>;
likewise the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> (Lords of Knowledge).

children.text: Ipv: bodhakartṛtāmayasyāpi bhedena viśvekṣaṇaṃ vidyeti ke cit / māyāśaktir apy eṣā vidyaiva / saṃsārottīrṇatvāt tatrasthā mantreśvaravidyeśvarāḥ //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: Some say that the perception of the universe through differentiation, even for one whose nature is awareness and agenthood, is <s>Vidyā</s>. This power of <s>Māyā</s> too is indeed <s>Vidyā</s>. Because they have transcended <s>saṃsāra</s>, those established therein are <s>Mantreśvaras</s> and <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>. //
The <s>Vidyā</s>-power reveals
the sovereignty of His essential nature in the state of a bound soul;
while that called <s>Māyā</s>
effects concealment.

children.text: Ipv: saṃsāriṇām aiśvaryasya svātmanaspratyabhijñānaṃ vidyayā, paśubhāvo māyayā //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: For those in <s>saṃsāra</s>, the recognition of the sovereignty of one's own Self is through <s>Vidyā</s>; the state of a bound soul is through <s>Māyā</s>. //
When difference, though of one flavor, appears,
and the non-Self is regarded as 'I',
whether as void, intellect, or body—
the power of <s>Māyā</s> expands.

children.text: Ipv: yadā bhāvā bhedenedaṃtayaiva bhāsante 'ham iti pramātṛtvena ca dehādis, tadā viparyadvayahetur māyāśaktir vimohinī nāma vibhor vijṛmbhate //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: When entities appear through differentiation, as 'this' alone, and when the body and such are regarded as the subject through the 'I'-sense, then the power of <s>Māyā</s>, called the deluding one, the cause of both perversions, expands from the Lord. //
And the knower who is void and such,
in relation to a knowable that is separate,
that knower, being himself the knowable, is wrapped
in the fivefold covering of <s>Kāla</s> (time) and the rest.

children.text: Ipv: yaś ca vyatiriktaprameyajāte pramātā śūnyādiḥ sa idam iti vedya eva vastutaḥ kālādyaiḥ pañcabhiś ca paratantrīkṛtaḥ / tatra kālād vartamānābhāsena tasya bhūtabahviṣyatsaṃbhavo, niyateḥ kāryakarmaphalaniyamo, rāgād bhogābhiṣvaṅgo, vidyākalābhyām, acidātmano 'svatantrasyāpīṣajjñānakriye citsvātantryarūpe //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: The knower who is void and so on, in relation to a separate class of knowables, is in reality himself a knowable object, made dependent by the five [coverings] beginning with <s>kāla</s> (time). Among these: by <s>kāla</s>, through the appearance of the present, his past and future existence; by <s>niyati</s>, the restriction of effect, action, and fruit; by <s>rāga</s>, attachment to enjoyments; by <s>vidyā</s> and <s>kalā</s>, even for the non-conscious and non-independent one, a modicum of knowledge and action that are in the nature of the freedom of consciousness. //
The knowable is twenty-three-fold,
consisting of effects and instruments;
its undifferentiated form, the one
<s>Pradhāna</s> (Primal Matter), is the root cause.
And here the series of external and internal organs
is thirteen-fold;
and the class of effects is ten-fold,
distinguished as gross and subtle.

children.text: Ipv: kāryāṇi dvidhā / śabdasparśarūparasagandhāni sūkṣmatvena tanmātrasaṃjñāni pañca, anyonyavyūhena sthūlāni pṛthivyādibuddhīndriyāṇi, vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthākhyāni pañca karmendriyāṇi, manobuddhyahaṅkārā iti tridhāntahkaraṇam iti trayoviṃśatibhedasya kāryakāraṇātmanaḥ prameyasya mūlabhūtaikāvibhāgadaśā prādhānākhyā //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: Effects are of two kinds. The five—sound, touch, form, taste, and smell—in their subtle form are called <s>tanmātras</s>. As mutual combinations in gross form, they are earth and so on. The five organs of knowledge, the five organs of action called speech, hands, feet, excretion, and generation, and the internal organ as threefold—<s>manas</s>, <s>buddhi</s>, and <s>ahaṃkāra</s>—thus the root state of undifferentiated unity of the knowable, consisting of effects and instruments in twenty-three divisions, is called <s>Pradhāna</s>. //
Thus ends the first lesson in the Chapter on Scriptural Testimony. //
Second Lesson //
Therein, in the state of mere subjectivity,
<s>Rudra</s> is the presiding deity;
in the expansion of differentiated knowables,
<s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> are established.

children.text: Ipv: śūnye puryaṣṭakātmake 'tyantasūkṣmadeha eva vā pramātṛmātre sthitav anyaprameyopasaṃhāre rudro 'dhiṣṭhātā, bhinnaprameyābhāse sargasthitihetū brahmaviṣṇū //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: In the state of the mere knower—in the void, in the body consisting of the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>), or in the extremely subtle body alone—when all other knowables are withdrawn, <s>Rudra</s> is the presiding deity. In the manifestation of differentiated knowables, <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> are the causes of creation and preservation. //
This knower, blinded by <s>Māyā</s>,
is the transmigrating soul, bound by <s>karma</s>;
when his sovereignty is made known by <s>Vidyā</s>,
dense with consciousness, he is called liberated.

children.text: Ipv: māyīyaśūnyāsipramātā niyatya karmādhīnaḥ saṃsārī, vidyāvaśād ātmatattvābhijñayā muktaḥ //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: The knower who is a void-like subject, dependent on <s>karma</s> through <s>niyati</s>, is a transmigrating soul; by the force of <s>Vidyā</s>, through the recognition of the true nature of the Self, he is liberated. //
When entities appear as His own limbs,
the knower is called the Lord (<s>Pati</s>);
when differentiated from Him due to <s>Māyā</s>,
tainted by afflictions, <s>karma</s>, and so on, he is a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>).

children.text: Ipv: aiśvaryadaśāyāṃ pramātā viśvaṃ śārīratayā paśyan patiḥ puṃstvāvasthāyāṃ tu rāgādikleśakarmavipākāśayaiḥ parītaḥ paśuḥ //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: In the state of sovereignty, the knower, seeing the universe as his body, is the Lord; but in the state of individuality, surrounded by afflictions such as <s>rāga</s>, <s>karma</s>, fruition, and latent impressions, he is a bound soul. //
The loss of freedom of awareness,
and the lack of awareness of freedom—
this twofold <s>āṇava mala</s> (impurity of finitude)
arises from the deprivation of one's own true nature.

children.text: Ipv: svatantro bodhaḥ paramārthas, tathārūpatvād eva pūrṇaḥ / tasya svātantryād eva tathecchayā svātantryaṃ vinā bodhamātranirmāṇe bodhitāṃ vinā svātantryamātranirmāṇe vā pūrṇatvābhāvena parimitatvād dvidhāṇutvaṃ tāttvikasvarūpaviparyāsān malatvam //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: Autonomous awareness is the ultimate reality; being of that very nature, it is complete. Of that, by its own freedom, by its own will, when awareness alone is produced without freedom, or when freedom alone is produced without awareness, there is finitude due to the absence of completeness—that is, limitation. This twofold finitude, being a perversion of the true essential nature, constitutes impurity (<s>mala</s>). //
In this very state, the manifestation of differentiated knowables—
that called <s>Māyā</s> gives birth and enjoyment;
when there is lack of awareness in the agent, there is <s>kārma</s> (karmic impurity);
but all three are through the power of <s>Māyā</s> alone.

children.text: Ipv: atraiva dvidhāṇave vedyam abhinnam api bhedena yadā bhāti tadāto 'pi viparyāsān nāmnā māyīyaṃ malam / ahetūnām api karmaṇāṃ janmādihetubhāvaviṣayaviparyāsād abodhātmakakartṛgataṃ kārmam / tanmalatrayanirmāṇe prabhor icchā māyāśaktir ucyate //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: In this very twofold finitude, when the knowable, though undifferentiated, appears as differentiated, that too is a perversion, and is called by name the <s>Māyīya mala</s> (impurity of Māyā). The perversion whereby even causeless actions become causes of birth and so on, residing in the agent who lacks awareness, is the <s>kārma mala</s> (karmic impurity). The Lord's will in the production of these three impurities is called the power of <s>Māyā</s>. //
Even though their nature is pure awareness,
those who lack supreme agenthood,
are created by the Lord as different from His own Self,
due to the loss of their agenthood.

children.text: Ipv: vedyānuparaktabodhānām api pūrṇakartṛtvaśūnyatvāt svarūpānyatvena prabhuṇā nirmāṇam //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: Even of those whose awareness is uncolored by the knowable, because they lack complete agenthood, their creation by the Lord as being other than His own nature occurs. //
Even though they share the single characteristic
of awareness, they are mutually different,
and that is through the differentiation of <s>Īśvara</s>'s will;
they are called <s>vijñānakevalins</s> (those with consciousness alone).

children.text: Ipv: śuddhabodhānāṃ bodhatvanityatvād\var{#nityatvād\lem \corr; #nityatvādh# \Ed} bhede 'py anyonyabhedas tathaiveśvareṇa nirmāṇān nānyathā / te ca sāṃkhyapuruṣaprāyā vijñānakevalā ity ucyate //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: Among pure awarenesses, despite having the common property of awareness and permanence, their mutual difference exists precisely because of creation by <s>Īśvara</s>, not otherwise. They are like the <s>puruṣas</s> of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and are called <s>vijñānakevalins</s>. //
But those of the nature of non-awareness, such as void,
are agents called <s>pralayākalas</s> (those without <s>kalā</s> at dissolution);
they also have karmic impurity,
but the <s>Māyīya</s> (impurity of Māyā) is constructed (conditional).

children.text: Ipv: śūnyaprāṇādau bodharūpatātikrameṇāhaṃtayā sthitāḥ pralayakevalinaḥ / teṣām aṇūnāṃ karmasaṃskāro 'py asti, māyāmalas tu vedyayogāyogābhyāṃ vikalpitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: Those established in the 'I'-sense, transcending the nature of awareness, in the void, <s>prāṇa</s>, and so on, are the <s>pralayakevalins</s>. These finite souls also have the karmic impression, but the <s>Māyā</s>-impurity is conditional upon the presence or absence of the knowable. //
Of awarenesses that also possess agenthood,
when the karmic impurity is destroyed,
and of those possessing differentiated knowables,
the <s>Māyā</s>-impurity—they are <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>.

children.text: Ipv: kartṛtāyoge 'pi bodhānāṃ karmottīrṇānāṃ vidyeśvaratve 'pi bhinnavedyayogān māyāmalam asty eva / pūrṇakartṛtvābhāvād īśvarād bhinnā anyonyaṃ ca pūrvavad ata evaiṣām aṇutvam api syāt //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: Even among awarenesses, though endowed with agenthood, even for those who have transcended <s>karma</s> and attained <s>Vidyeśvara</s>-hood, the <s>Māyā</s>-impurity persists due to the association with differentiated knowables. Due to the absence of complete agenthood, they are different from <s>Īśvara</s> and from one another, as before. Hence, even they have finitude. //
And for all beings, from gods downward,
the impurity is threefold;
among these, the karmic impurity alone
is the primary cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration).

children.text: Ipv: devādīnāṃ sthāvarāntānāṃ saṃsāriṇāṃ trayo 'pi malāḥ, kārma eva saṃsāraprayojakaḥ //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: For transmigrating beings from gods down to immovable things, all three impurities exist; the karmic one alone is the instigator of <s>saṃsāra</s>. //
And this reality of mind (<s>citta-tattva</s>),
consisting of agenthood, empowered by <s>Kalā</s>,
for the non-conscious void and such,
abides in a limited way as a subordinate attribute.

children.text: Ipv: saṃsāriṇām etac ca cittattvaṃ kartṛtārūpaṃ śūnyaprāṇādau jaḍe devasya kalāśaktyopodbalyamānam upasarjanatvenāvasthānāt parimitam / ataś cātraiva mukhyam aṇutvam //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: For transmigrating beings, this <s>citta-tattva</s> (mind-reality), which has the form of agenthood, being empowered by the <s>Kalā</s>-power of the Lord in the inert void, <s>prāṇa</s>, and so on, subsists in a subordinate position and is therefore limited. Hence it is here precisely that finitude is primary. //
And the primacy of agenthood
and of awareness belongs to the conscious Self;
in the void and such, which are its subordinate attributes, knowledge
has the character of absorption in that power.

children.text: Ipv: etad eva punaḥ śūnyādi kartṛtātmano bodhasya yadopasarjanatvenāste tadāsya pramātur etad bodhamayatām āpannasya jñānaṃ tacchaktisamāveśalakṣaṇam ucyate //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: This very void and so on—when it subsists as a subordinate attribute of agenthood, which is of the nature of awareness—then, for this knower who has attained the nature of awareness, the knowledge is said to have the character of absorption in that power. //
In the void, whose nature is the absence of intellect and such,
in the domain of 'I'-consciousness and agenthood,
consisting of merely indistinct impressions
without form, there is voidness of the knowable.

children.text: Ipv: buddhiprāṇādiniṣedhamātre yadāhaṃtābhimānena pramātṛtā tadā sauṣupte tāvanmātrāvasthitau vedyābhāvaḥ saṃskārasya saṃbhave 'py arūpatvenānupalakṣyatvāt / tāvataiva sāṃkhyapuruṣād viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: When, in the mere negation of intellect, <s>prāṇa</s>, and so on, subjectivity consists of the 'I'-sense conceit, then in that state of deep sleep, limited to just that, there is the absence of the knowable, since, even though the <s>saṃskāra</s> (impression) may exist, it is unperceived due to its formlessness. It is by this much alone that there is a distinction from the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> <s>puruṣa</s>. //
The inner activity of the senses
is considered to propel <s>prāṇa</s> and so on,
and is called life; or alternatively, in <s>prāṇa</s>,
the 'I'-sense consisting of the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>).

children.text: Ipv: eṣa eva śūnyapramātā sarvendriyaśaktisādhāraṇajīvanākhyaprāṇādipreraṇāntarvṛttir jīvākhyas, tāsām indriyaśaktīnām ahaṃtayā saha puryaṣṭakatvam athavā prāṇāhaṃtayā pramātṛtvena puryaṣṭakatā //
children.translated_text: Vṛtti: This very void-knower, whose inner activity propels <s>prāṇa</s> and so on, being the common ground of all the powers of the senses, is called by the name 'life' (<s>jīva</s>). The <s>puryaṣṭaka</s>-nature of those sense-powers together with the 'I'-sense, or alternatively the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s>-nature through the subjectivity of the <s>prāṇa</s>-'I'-sense. //
In the state of mere [limited consciousness],
the state of deep sleep, resembling <s>pralaya</s> (cosmic dissolution), has been described,
with or without an object of experience,
with or without the impurity of <s>Māyā</s>.

children.text: Ipv: śūnyatāyāṃ sthitau vedyābhāvān māyāmalābhāvaḥ, prāṇādau sukhasparśādivedyayogān māyāmalavat pralaya iva sauṣuptaṃ padam //
children.translated_text: In the state of the void, due to the absence of objects of experience, there is absence of the impurity of <s>Māyā</s>. In the state of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, due to connection with objects of experience such as pleasure and touch, the state of deep sleep is like <s>pralaya</s> (dissolution), as if accompanied by the impurity of <s>Māyā</s>. //
Even in the path of mind alone, due to the delusion
of appearing as objects of the senses,
the vivid manifestation of things —
this creation is considered the state of dream.

children.text: Ipv: cakṣurādīndriyaśaktyapravṛttav api manaḥśaktyaiva dṛṣṭarūpādyābhāseśvarasṛṣṭir aṇoḥ svapnapadam / anyapramātṛsādhāraṇarūpādyābhāsānuvṛttitaḥ kālāntarānanuvṛtter bhrāntir eṣā //
children.translated_text: Even without the activity of the powers of the sense organs such as the eye, through the power of mind alone, the <s>Īśvara</s>-creation for the <s>aṇu</s> (limited self) consisting of manifestations of previously seen forms and the like is the dream state. Because the manifestations of forms and the like, which are common to other knowing subjects, recur, yet do not recur at other times, this is delusion. //
That creation which, by being the object of all senses,
is stable as external,
and common to all
knowing subjects — that is the waking state.

children.text: Ipv: sarvāntarbahiḥkaraṇaśaktyā sṛṣṭir jāgarā, tatrāpi pūrvavad dvicandrādibhrāntiḥ //
children.translated_text: Creation through the power of all internal and external instruments is the waking state. There too, delusion such as seeing double moons occurs as before. //
This triad, beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>, is to be abandoned,
because of the predominance of the quality of agency [being diminished],
consisting mainly in the decrease and increase of that [sovereignty],
through connection with pleasure, pain, and the like.

children.text: Ipv: etāni jāgarasvapnasuṣuptāni prāṇāder ātmatvenābhimanyamānasyodrekāt svātantryasyāpahrāsād dheyāni, svātantryasya mātrayopacayaḥ sukhaharṣādayas tathaiva nyūnatā duḥkhadveṣādayaḥ / sarvabhogātmā saṃsāro bandhaḥ //
children.translated_text: These states of waking, dream, and deep sleep are to be abandoned because of the excess of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest being identified as the self, and because of the diminishment of <s>svātantrya</s> (sovereignty). The increase of sovereignty by a degree constitutes pleasure, joy, and the like; likewise its decrease constitutes pain, aversion, and the like. <s>Saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), consisting of all experience, is bondage. //
<s>Prāṇa</s> (the vital breath) consists of <s>prāṇa</s> (inhalation) and <s>apāna</s> (exhalation),
respectively in the states of sleep and waking.
That which has the nature of the cessation of both is called <s>samāna</s>,
in deep sleep, as at the equinoxes.

children.text: Ipv: sa ca prāṇātmā [svapne] prāṇāpānarūpaśvāsapraśvāsarūpo jāgare 'tha supte [atra] tayor api viṣuvatīva rātridinayoḥ sāmye tannyūnatādhikyarodhāt samānasaṃjñaḥ //
children.translated_text: And that vital self in dream has the form of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, that is, inhalation and exhalation, in the waking state; and in sleep, like the equinoxes between night and day, when both are in equilibrium, due to the cessation of the decrease and increase of those two, it is called <s>samāna</s>. //
Rising upward through the middle, it is called <s>udāna</s>,
moving in the <s>turya</s> (fourth state), having the nature of fire.
<s>Vijñānākala</s> and <s>Mantreśa</s> —
<s>vyāna</s>, the supreme, has a universal nature.

children.text: Ipv: prāṇāpānayoḥ pārśvadvayatiryakpravāhavicchedenaikatām āpādyordhvarūpamadhyamārgapravāheṇodgamanād udānaḥ / madhyanetram ivordhvabhāktvād agnidharmā turyadaśāyām / turyātīte dikkālānavacchede pūrṇe pravāhatāṃ hitvātinirbharāvastho vyānasaṃjñaḥ / etac ca daśādvayam upādeyaṃ prāṇaśakteḥ parameśvarakalpatvenāvasthānāt //
children.translated_text: By cutting off the lateral and transverse flow of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> on both sides, unifying them through rising by the upward middle path, it becomes <s>udāna</s>. Because it rises upward like the central eye, it has the nature of fire, in the state of <s>turya</s> (the fourth). In <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth), when fullness is attained without limitation of space and time, abandoning the state of flow and becoming supremely replete, it is called <s>vyāna</s>. And this pair of states is to be embraced, because the <s>prāṇa</s>-power abides as equivalent to <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord). //
Thus ends the second chapter of the <s>Āgamādhikāra</s> (Section on Scripture). //
Thus ends the <s>Āgamādhikāra</s>. //
4. <s>Tattvasaṃgrahādhikāra</s> (Chapter on the Synthesis of Principles) //
One's own Self alone, of all living beings,
is the one <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord),
whose form is the universe, nourished by the undivided
awareness 'I am this.'

children.text: Ipv: ekaḥ prathamopādeyaturyadaśāyām akhaṇḍitagrāhakākhaṇḍitagrāhyatanmelanācamatkāropabṛṃhitaḥ sādhāraṇa eva sarvaprāṇinām ātmā viśvarūpo maheśvaraḥ //
children.translated_text: In the primary state of <s>turya</s> (the fourth) that is to be attained, the one Self of all living beings, universal in form, is <s>Maheśvara</s>, nourished by the <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic rapture) arising from the unbroken fusion of unbroken subject and unbroken object — this is common [to all]. //
In the object-portion of His own creation,
through the nature of the intellect and other apprehending subjects,
that [universe] has been brought to the condition
of being grasped by <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-sense).

children.text: Ipv: maheśvarasya jṛmbhāmaye 'smin nirgate tasminn idaṃtāparāmarśe grāhyaṃ yan nirmitaṃ buddhiḥ prāṇo 'tha śūnyaṃ tad vedyaikadeśarūpam ahaṃkārāvamṛśyatāpādanena paricchinnagrāhakīkṛtam //
children.translated_text: In this expansion of <s>Maheśvara</s>'s play, in that emergent awareness of 'this-ness' as the object, whatever has been created — the intellect, <s>prāṇa</s>, and the void — being of the nature of a portion of the knowable, has been made into a limited subject by being brought under the grasp of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-consciousness). //
The individual soul, consisting of non-recognition
of one's own true nature, is considered manifold.
There, in creation, action and bliss —
experience is of the nature of pain and pleasure.

children.text: Ipv: etad eva viśvātmanaḥ parimitatvakaraṇam apratyabhijñānam ucyate / evaṃ cānekabuddhiprāṇādikhaṇḍagatāparāhaṃkāraparāmarśaḥ parāparijñānasaṃjñaḥ / pratyakātmano bahavas, teṣu pramātṛrūpeṣu maheśvareṇa svānandaḥ svakriyaikakartṛtānusāriṇī nirmitā / sa eva bhoga ānandaleśākhyaḥ sukhasaṃjñitaḥ kriyālavātmā duḥkharūpaḥ kriyā duḥkhaṃ ca vakṣyate //
children.translated_text: This very non-recognition is said to be what makes the universal Self limited. And thus the awareness of ego grasped in fragmented portions of the manifold intellect, <s>prāṇa</s>, and the rest, is called non-recognition of the Supreme. The individual selves are many; in them, as knowing subjects, <s>Maheśvara</s> has created His own bliss following the agency of His own action alone. That very experience, called a fraction of bliss, is designated as pleasure; that which has the nature of a trace of action is pain. Action and pain will be explained [further]. //
The knowledge and action of the Lord
with respect to things that are His own limbs —
in the third [level], that of <s>Māyā</s>, these very same
become <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> for the bound soul.

children.text: Ipv: īśvarasya jñānakriye te māyayā sahite paśoḥ sattvarajastamāṃsi //
children.translated_text: The knowledge and action of <s>Īśvara</s>, when conjoined with <s>Māyā</s>, become <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> for the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul). //
For these <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), which undergo transformation
into instruments and effects,
the designation of being powers is not given,
since they abide in differentiation.

children.text: Ipv: sattvarajastamasāṃ ca bhedenāvabhāsān na śaktivyapadeśaḥ śaktiśaktimator abhedāt / vastutaḥ śaktivikāso viśvam //
children.translated_text: Because <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> manifest in differentiation, they are not designated as powers, since power and the possessor of power are non-different. In reality, the universe is the unfolding of power. //
The bliss of being and action belong to the Lord;
the absence of that also is that [power] for the bound soul.
Both together constitute <s>rajas</s>; pain
is adhesive, consisting of <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: Ipv: īśvarasyānantakartṛtā camatkārarūpā kriyoktā paramaprakāśānandamayī, pratyagātmanas tu tau prakāśānandau grāhyabhūtau sattvam ucyate / tadabhāvaś ca tamaḥ, sattvatamasī prakāśānandatadabhāvarūpe dve api śleṣātmanī [rajaḥ] / paśoḥ rajaḥsaṃjñayā kriyā ca duḥkhaṃ cocyate //
children.translated_text: The infinite agency of <s>Īśvara</s>, having the form of <s>camatkāra</s> (rapturous wonder), is called action — it is of the nature of supreme light and bliss. But for the individual self, those two — light and bliss — being objects of experience, are called <s>sattva</s>. And the absence of that is <s>tamas</s>. <s>Sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>, whose natures are light-and-bliss and the absence thereof, are both adhesive in nature [constituting <s>rajas</s>]. For the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul), what is called <s>rajas</s> is both action and pain. //
Those [manifestations] of the Lord that are
not based on conventional 'this'-awareness,
they [appear as] mixed and differentiated,
and thus manifesting variously.

children.text: Ipv: ye caite maheśvarasyedaṃśabdasaṃketānusaṃdhānaṃ vināpi prakāśasya parāmarśasāratvād bāladaśāyām ivedamarthanirdeśyā bhāvās, te 'nekābhāsasāmānādhikaraṇyena svalakṣaṇātmanaḥ pṛthaksāmānyarūpatayā nānākārāś ca tathā tannirmāṇāt prathante //
children.translated_text: And those things of <s>Maheśvara</s> that, even without the deliberate linking of the word 'this' in conventional designation, are indicative of object-meaning by virtue of consciousness being essentially awareness — as in the state of infancy — they, through the co-presence of manifold appearances, as particulars having their own defining characteristics and separately as universals, manifest in various forms, because they are so created. //
But those objects, having differentiated appearances,
are to be constructed by the individual self,
with their respective distinct names,
in the domain of memory, imagination, and the like.

children.text: Ipv: te vibhinnāvabhāsāḥ sāmānyātmano 'rthās tadanubhavasaṃskṛtaiḥ kṛśo 'haṃ duḥkhī sukhī vāham iti vicitravyapadeśaviṣayīkriyamāṇātmabhiḥ kṣetrajñair vikalpanaśaktyā tattadghaṭarajataśuklapaṭaśakaṭādināmnāntaspratyavamarśanīyatvena pradarśyante smṛtau pūrvānubhavāpramoṣe, vicitrotprekṣādiṣu tu svātantryeṇa / ayam eva grāhyagrāhakabhedāvabhāsaḥ śabdamayaḥ paśubhāve saṃsārabandhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Those objects having differentiated appearances, being of the nature of universals, are displayed by the <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (individual knowers) — who have been impressed by the experience of those [objects] and who are made the subjects of various designations such as 'I am thin,' 'I am suffering,' 'I am happy' — through the power of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction), as internally apprehensible under the respective names such as pot, silver, white cloth, cart, and so forth, in memory (the non-loss of prior experience), and in various imaginative constructions and the like through [the exercise of] freedom. This very manifestation of the differentiation of subject and object, pervaded by language, is the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s> in the state of the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul). //
The individual creation of that [bound soul],
dependent on the creation of the Lord,
this too, through ignorance, by the real
power of entry of that [Lord's] nature,
by obstructing rest in one's own [true] Self,
through the restless, <s>prāṇa</s>-natured,
activity of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction),
having the form of the diversity of various phonemes —

children.text: Ipv: kṣetraś ceśvararūpa eva tattatsāmānyarūpānarthān īśaśaktyaivāparijñātayā sarvasādhāraṇārthadarśanasaṃskṛtānanyavedyān nirmimīte / sā ceśvaraśāktiḥ svātmamātraviśrāntivirodhāya māyāvyapadeśyā tattatkakārādivarṇabhedaśatānantagaṇanā prāṇarūpeṇa cañcalatām āpannā vikalpākhyavyāpārā tathāntaḥ sṛjaty arthān //
children.translated_text: The <s>kṣetrajña</s> (individual knower), who is indeed of the nature of <s>Īśvara</s>, creates inwardly the various objects having the nature of universals through <s>Īśvara</s>'s own power that remains unrecognized, [objects that are] unknowable apart from [being] conditioned by the perception of objects common to all, [known only through that power]. And that power of <s>Īśvara</s>, to be designated as <s>Māyā</s>, obstructing rest in one's own Self alone, counting hundreds and endless varieties of distinct phonemes such as 'ka' and the rest, having assumed restlessness through the nature of <s>prāṇa</s>, is the operation called <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) — thus it creates objects inwardly. //
The creation of the Lord is common [to all] and also otherwise,
because of vivid manifestation.
Through the gradual abandonment of <s>vikalpa</s> and one-pointedness,
the state of <s>Īśvara</s> (Lordship) is [attained] step by step.

children.text: Ipv: īśvarasya tu sṛṣṭiḥ sarvapramātṝṇāṃ sādhāraṇī teṣāṃ tanmadhya evotpādād, ekapramātṛniyatā caikapramātrāveśena svapnabhrāntyādau sṛṣṭiḥ / sā cāham idam ity etāvat parāmarśamayī bhedānudayād vikalpojjhitā spaṣṭāvabhāsā ca / tatrāntarāntarodyatkṣetrajñavyāpāravikalpananirhrāsapariśīlanena saṃsāriṇāṃ krameṇaikarasaiśvaryodgamāt kṣetrajñatāvimuktiḥ //
children.translated_text: The creation of <s>Īśvara</s> is common to all knowing subjects, since they arise within that very [creation]; and it is also confined to a single knowing subject through the entry into a single subject, as in dream, delusion, and the like. And that [creation] consists only of the awareness 'I am this,' free from <s>vikalpa</s> since differentiation does not arise, and is vivid in manifestation. There, through the gradual cultivation of diminishing the <s>vikalpa</s>-activity of the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (individual knower) that intermittently arises, there is liberation from the state of being a <s>kṣetrajña</s> through the gradual emergence of the unified sovereignty of <s>saṃsārins</s> (transmigrating beings). //
'All this splendor is mine' —
for one who knows thus,
even in the activity of <s>vikalpas</s> (conceptual constructions),
there is the state of <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord), since [one is] of universal nature.

children.text: Ipv: kṣetrajñasyāpīśvaraśāktyaiva vikalpārambha iti taddaśāyām api parijñāteśvarabhāvasya mamāyaṃ saṃsāramayo vibhava ity abhedena viśvam āviśataḥ parāmarśamātrān aśeṣān vikalpān saṃpādayato maheśvarataiva //
children.translated_text: Since the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (individual knower) too initiates <s>vikalpa</s> through <s>Īśvara</s>'s power alone, even in that state, for one who has recognized the nature of <s>Īśvara</s>, who enters the universe in non-difference [thinking] 'this splendor consisting of <s>saṃsāra</s> is mine,' who accomplishes all <s>vikalpas</s> through mere awareness — there is indeed the state of <s>Maheśvara</s>. //
The liberated one regards the common knowable
as non-different from one's own Self,
as does <s>Maheśvara</s>; the bound one,
however, [regards it] as utterly different.

children.text: Ipv: baddhamuktayor vedyam ekaṃ, kiṃ tu baddho 'tyantavibhedena tad vetti vimuktaḥ svātmadehatvena //
children.translated_text: The knowable is the same for both the bound and the liberated. However, the bound one knows it in utter differentiation, while the liberated one [knows it] as the body of one's own Self. //
But in every way, when [all objects] are dissolved within,
replete with the flood of infinite principles,
<s>Śiva</s> [is realized as] a mass of consciousness and bliss,
whose body is the supreme imperishable.

children.text: Ipv: sarvathā tv antarlīne prameye 'haṃmatau pūrṇāyāṃ śivataiva //
children.translated_text: But in every way, when the knowable is dissolved within and the 'I'-awareness is full, there is nothing but the state of <s>Śiva</s>. //
Thus, knowing the Self of this [universe],
and likewise [knowing] its right knowledge and action,
seeing as one desires,
one [truly] knows and acts.

children.text: Ipv: ittham āviṣkṛtaśaktyabhijñānam ātmānam anantajñānakriyāśaktinibhṛtam īśvaraṃ pratyabhijñāya yathecchaṃ sarvaṃ paśyati nirmimīte //
children.translated_text: Thus, having recognized the Self — <s>Īśvara</s>, replete with infinite powers of knowledge and action — whose powers have been revealed, one sees everything as one wishes and creates [at will]. //

children.text: iti prakaṭito mayā sughaṭa eṣa mārgo navo
children.translated_text: Thus this new yet easy path has been set forth by me,
as was taught by the great <s>Guru</s> in the <s>Śivadṛṣṭi</s> scripture.

children.text: tad atra nidadhat padaṃ bhuvanakartṛtām ātmano
children.translated_text: One who, placing one's foot on this [path], contemplates the creatorship of the universe
as belonging to one's own Self, as being of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, constantly entering [that state], attains perfection.

children.text: Ipv: yatra yathāvasthita eva vyavahāre pratyabhijñāmātrāc chivatālābhaḥ / sa ayam avakra evābhinavo mārgaḥ sākṣātkṛtaparameśvarabhaṭṭārakākārair bhaṭṭaśrīsomānandapādaiḥ śivadṛṣṭināmni prakaraṇe nirdiṣṭo mayā yuktinibandhanena hṛdayaṃgamīkṛtaḥ / etat pariśīlanena śivatāveśāj jīvann eva mukto bhavati //
children.translated_text: Wherein, remaining exactly as one is in ordinary life, through mere <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition) alone, the attainment of <s>Śiva</s>-nature [is achieved]. This very direct and new path was taught by <s>Bhaṭṭa Śrī Somānandapāda</s>, whose form is that of the directly realized <s>Parameśvara Bhaṭṭāraka</s> (Supreme Lord), in the treatise called <s>Śivadṛṣṭi</s>, and has been made accessible to the heart by me through reasoned demonstration. Through the cultivation of this, by entering into the state of <s>Śiva</s>, one becomes liberated even while living. //

children.text: tais tair apy upayācitair upanatas tanvyāḥ sthito 'py antike
children.translated_text: Just as a husband, though entreated with various [offerings] and standing close

children.text: kānto lokasamāna evam aparijñāto na rantuṃ yathā
children.translated_text: to his slender [wife], when unrecognized is like any common man and unable to give delight,
so too, this Self of all, the Lord of the universe, whose qualities are unexamined by the world,
is not sufficient for [bestowing] its own glory — therefore this <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition) has arisen.
Through the analogy of the husband, the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition of the Lord) is to be established, and it has an unprecedented fruit. //
For the effortless attainment of people,
by the son of <s>Udayākara</s>,
this <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition of the Lord)
has been set forth by <s>Utpala</s>.
This easily accessible path to perfection has been demonstrated. //
Thus ends the <s>Tattvasaṃgrahādhikāra</s> (Chapter on the Synthesis of Principles). //

body.translated_text: // Thus concludes the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñāvṛtti</s> (Commentary on the Recognition of the Lord). //
